ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.11 Ryde voucher to the rider under NS-7 for the unexempt off-route kilometres on segment F3; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file but take no account action (RD-6 not triggered).
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so fare follows the meter and extra kilometres enter the fare; RD-1 is satisfied by a single off-route segment, F3 (23:03–23:14, 7.28 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.25 km, +5.04 km, up to 2060 m off the optimal route), and the trace marks that element ✓ [F3][F7][RD-1]. No clause exempts the segment. RD-4(a) is marked ✗: F15 records no traffic incident near the route in the trip window, and RD-4(b) speed-band records are corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment on their own [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

The RD-5 consent question turns on what the rider actually agreed to. F8 (driver, 22:59) asks a specific named-road question — "Jam on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road?" — and F9 (rider, 23:00) answers "Sure, no problem.", sent before the segment started at 23:03 [F3][F8][F9]. Read in context this is a specific named-road authorisation reaching only driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road, not a general "whichever way is fastest" licence [RD-5]. The record does not merely fail to tie the segment to the named road, it places it elsewhere: the driver's own post-trip statement F11 says "In the end I went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it looked clearer" [F11]. Where the record places the segment somewhere other than the agreed road, the agreement to that road does not cover it, so under RD-5 the consent ground is "named_road_elsewhere" and the finding is counts (not undetermined) — the fact table carries no road name for the driven path, but F11 supplies a place name of the driver's own, which is exactly the situation the rule addresses [F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

RD-3 does not exempt anything: no rider message named a place, and no stop is measured in the segment, so the rider-named-stop branch is not engaged [F8][F9][RD-3]. The one unexempt segment therefore falls to RD-2. The rate is taken from the fare record as the trace states it: this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km = $1.4102/km [F4]. Amount: 5.04 km (F3) × $1.4102/km = $7.1086 → $7.11 [F3][F4][RD-2]. I do not refund the difference between F4's billed excess $7.50 (5.32 km) and the segment's 5.04 km, nor the fare-excess km outside any measured segment; and the $0.11 metered waiting unit (F5) and the published base/platform lines in F7 are not routing items, so nothing further is recoverable [F5][F7][RD-2][RD-3][FARE-1].

No account flag attaches. RD-6 requires both that the case is upheld against the driver and that the profile shows an already-upheld route dispute in the 90-day window; F18 shows 1 upheld dispute but route: 0, so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and the precondition fails — the trace marks this element ✗ [F18][RD-6]. F17/F18 are profile facts and cannot decide the case or the flag in any event [F17][F18][RD-6].

No rider message named a place and no stop is measured, so RD-3 does not exempt it [F8][F9][F11][F3][RD-5][RD-3].

rejected_claims.reason: The overrun is real (F1, F2, F3, F7) but RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segments' extra_km at this trip's rate; C1 asks for the whole shortfall while only the single F3 segment (5.04 km) is unexempt, so the larger figure is not recoverable [F1][F2][F3][F7][RD-2].

Accepted in part: F11 does show the driver drove a road other than the one he named, but it is a post-trip statement and not rider consent (G11); the operative finding rests on F8/F9's scope plus F11's placement of the segment elsewhere [F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

Correct that consent does not cover the driven segment, but the finding is 'counts' (named road agreed, record places the segment elsewhere), not 'undetermined': F11 names another road, so the record settles it [F3][F11][RD-5].

Accepted: RD-4(a) is not met (F15 no incident) and RD-4(b) bands cannot exempt alone; but C4's dismissal of F12 is immaterial to the outcome, which turns on RD-5 scope, not on traffic [F12][F15][RD-4].

The billed excess F4 ($7.50 for 5.32 km) is larger than the recoverable amount; RD-2 refunds only unexempt segment extra_km, and the 13.3 km estimate is not a fixed quote on this metered trip [F1][F4][F7][RD-2].

The 5.04 × $1.4102 = $7.11 figure is granted, but the request that 'any routing item wrongly added' fall is rejected: the $0.11 meter waiting unit (F5) is chargeable and non-refundable on RydeTAXI and surge is already 1.0× with no line to remove [F3][F4][F5][F6][RD-2][RD-3][FARE-1].

RD-6's flag precondition is not met: F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (the one upheld dispute was not a route case), and the rider's clean profile F17 cannot establish the driver's breach [F17][F18][RD-6].
F9 is not a general route choice: it answers F8's specific named-road question, so under RD-5 it covers Upper Paya Lebar Road only, and F11 places the driven segment elsewhere [F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

Rejected as to outcome: agreement to a named road is not merely 'undetermined' where F11 supplies a place name for the driven segment — the record places it off the agreed road, so it counts [F3][F11][RD-5].

Rejected: RD-4(b) speed-band corroboration cannot exempt a segment on its own (RD-4 explicitly says so), and the driver's stated reason was that the alternative 'looked clearer' (F11), not a recorded event [F11][F12][F13][F14][RD-4][RD-5].
Accepted as far as it goes and it supports the outcome: no RD-4(a) basis exists (F15), so the segment is sized under RD-2 [F3][F15][RD-4][RD-2].
Accepted: F3 is a genuine deviation beyond noise and weather cannot explain it (F16); nothing in it shifts the amount below the RD-2 figure [F3][F16][RD-1][RD-2].
Accepted; the cap of 5.04 × $1.4102 = $7.11 is the amount awarded [F3][F4][F7][RD-2].
Accepted: the $0.11 metered waiting unit and the base/platform lines are not refundable; this narrows, and does not enlarge, the rider's recovery [F5][F7][RD-3][FARE-1].
Accepted: the estimate is not a fixed quote and a full fare refund would exceed RD-2; the rider was awarded only the unexempt mileage [F1][F2][F4][F7][RD-2][FARE-1].
Agreed: nothing in F8–F11 is a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no safety escalation is warranted [F8][F9][F10][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].
Accepted: F18 shows route: 0 with the single upheld dispute not route-related, so RD-6's precondition fails and no flag_account attaches [F18][RD-6].
